titleEn: AI cameras catch cow lameness early, cut antibiotic use 41%
titleZh: AI摄像头早期检测奶牛跛行，抗生素使用减少41%
summaryZh: 新西兰公司Herd-i利用安装在挤奶厅出口的AI摄像头，在每次挤奶时自动评估奶牛的步态和体况评分，帮助牧场主早期发现跛行等健康问题。独立分析显示，该系统使需要跛行治疗的奶牛减少38%，跛行相关抗生素治疗减少41%。该技术已进入美国市场，并推出“创始农场”计划招募25个农场免费安装试用。文章介绍了技术原理、数据基础、农场效益及未来拓展方向，对智慧畜牧从业者具有重要参考价值。
featuredReason: 该报道详细介绍了AI摄像头在奶牛跛行和体况评分中的实际应用及显著经济效益（抗生素减少41%），并提供了美国市场准入和试用计划的具体信息，对智慧畜牧从业者了解前沿技术落地和商业机会具有直接参考价值。

AI cameras catch cow lameness early, cut antibiotic use 41%

New Zealand-based company enters the U.S. dairy market with technology that scores lameness and body condition at every milking.

Elizabeth Hodges,staff writer,Farm ProgressNovember 5, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

Dairy farmers are turning to camera technology like Herd-i to monitor herd health and ease labor demands on the farm. Elizabeth Hodges 

link

Labor shortage is always a hot topic of conversation across agriculture sectors. Whether the cause is politics, generational shifts or other factors, new technologies are stepping up to serve as an extra set of eyes on the farm.

The dairy industry is often described as an early adopter of technology, from aggressive record-keeping to advanced genetics to robotics assisting on the farm. This demanding industry requires top-of-the-line tools to stay competitive.

Complementing recent developments in virtual fencing collars that record individual cow data, Herd-i brings a new piece of technology to the farm.

Herd-i’s camera system is installed at the exit of a milking parlor. Each time a cow passes through after milking, the cameras capture two data points: locomotion and body condition score (BCS).

“The technology is 4½ years old in New Zealand, and we have over 119,000 cows that are currently being scored every single milking,” said Nicole Mozeliak, CEO of Herd-i U.S. “We’ve just entered the U.S. market with this technology.”

Related:Is your beef-on-dairy calf getting enough colostrum?

Boosting farm efficiency

As cows exit the milking parlor, Herd-i’s cameras capture video footage of each animal that is then uploaded to the cloud. Machine learning models, trained using assessments from veterinary and BCS experts, analyze and assign individual locomotion and BCS. By tracking these scores over time, the system helps farmers identify subtle changes in gait and condition that might otherwise go unnoticed.

Through a customizable dashboard, producers can tailor what information they see.

“Farmers can set their own thresholds, and the system identifies cows requiring attention. That means they can focus on specific animals, whether that’s drafting a cow for further assessment or making more targeted management decisions,” Mozeliak said.

She said the data is reliable because of the groundwork laid before the technology launched commercially in New Zealand.

“Our lameness scoring was built on over half a million videos that were scored and trained by veterinarians, and then the body condition scoring was founded by 1.1 million camera views by expert assessors,” Mozeliak said. “So, we believe that the technology has been proven, and we have it in existence, and we have dairy farmers in New Zealand who’ve been telling us how amazing it is and the difference that it’s made.”

From a truck, tractor cab or anywhere in the world, farmers can check in on their herd through videos collected after each cow leaves a milking session. Those videos also can be shared with veterinarians, farm employees or anyone else who might need to act on early detection signals.

Related:The $345-per-cow opportunity in your milk tank

According to Mozeliak, an independent analysis by a New Zealand agricultural consultancy examined three dairy seasons before and after Herd-i was installed at Darnley Dairy. The study found a 38% reduction in cows requiring lameness treatment and a 41% reduction in antibiotic treatments specifically for lameness. That equated to an average of 82 fewer cows requiring treatment and 40 fewer antibiotic treatments per season.

“We all know that when you can get to a cow faster and provide a less invasive, less costly treatment, their ability to produce is kept intact, and as a result, there’s more milk in the vat,” Mozeliak said.

Mozeliak said Herd-i not only keeps a farm’s finances moving in a positive direction but also can reduce mental stress, especially during busy seasons.

Incorporating innovation

Following its U.S. launch in September, Herd-i is offering a Founding Farmer program. Through the program, 25 farms will receive complimentary installation and a discounted subscription rate.

In exchange, Herd-i is looking for feedback to help refine the technology for U.S. dairies and shape the product’s future.

“We’re looking for those farmers who not only are excited to take the lameness and BCS product to their farm, but to also help be an ambassador. Those relationships matter,” Mozeliak said.

Related:Robots don’t replace good dairy management

The program mirrors one in New Zealand, where a group of farmers helped shape how the technology addresses on-farm challenges.

While the technology is currently designed for dairy cattle, Mozeliak said she sees potential for it to eventually serve the beef cattle industry as well.

“The future of Herd-i is bright in terms of the conversations with farmers. They are very interested in additional information related to heat, temperature and weight,” Mozeliak said. “A lot of those things are something that they have to track manually right now.”

By automating these tasks, producers have shown strong interest in this technology. Whether the human eye misses these subtle cues or farms simply lack the labor to spare, these cameras can fill a void on the operation.

Farmers interested in learning more about Herd-i or joining the Founding Farmer program can visit herd-i.com.

About the Author

Elizabeth Hodges

staff writer, Farm Progress

Growing up on a third-generation purebred Berkshire hog operation, Elizabeth Hodges of Julian, Neb., credits her farm background for showing her what it takes to be involved in the ag industry. She began her journalism career in high school, reporting on producer progress for the Midwest Messenger newspaper.

While a student at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, she became a Husker Harvest Days intern at Nebraska Farmer in 2022. The next year, she was hired full-time as a staff writer for Farm Progress. Elizabeth graduated from UNL in 2024 with a double major in Agriculture and Environmental Sciences Communication and Animal Science.Hodges’ father, Michael, raises purebred Berkshire hogs, and her mother, Christy, is an ag education teacher and FFA advisor at Johnson County Central. Hodges is the oldest sibling of four.

translationZh:
劳动力短缺一直是农业各领域的热门话题。无论是政治因素、代际更替还是其他原因，新技术正在成为农场上的“额外一双眼睛”。

奶牛业常被视为技术的早期采用者，从积极的记录管理到先进的遗传学，再到机器人辅助农场作业。这个要求苛刻的行业需要顶尖工具来保持竞争力。

作为对近期虚拟围栏项圈（可记录单头奶牛数据）发展的补充，Herd-i为农场带来了一项新技术。

Herd-i的摄像头系统安装在挤奶厅出口处。每头奶牛挤奶后经过时，摄像头会捕捉两个数据点：运动能力和体况评分（BCS）。

“这项技术在新西兰已有四年半历史，目前我们有超过119,000头奶牛在每次挤奶时被评分，”Herd-i美国公司CEO Nicole Mozeliak说。“我们刚刚带着这项技术进入美国市场。”

**提升农场效率**

当奶牛走出挤奶厅时，Herd-i的摄像头会捕捉每头动物的视频片段，然后上传到云端。机器学习模型利用兽医和体况评分专家的评估进行训练，分析并给出个体运动能力和体况评分。通过长期跟踪这些分数，系统帮助牧场主识别可能被忽视的步态和体况细微变化。

通过可定制的仪表盘，生产者可以调整他们看到的信息。

“牧场主可以设定自己的阈值，系统会识别需要关注的奶牛。这意味着他们可以专注于特定动物，无论是将某头奶牛挑选出来进行进一步评估，还是做出更有针对性的管理决策，”Mozeliak说。

她表示，数据可靠是因为技术在新西兰商业化推出之前做了大量基础工作。

“我们的跛行评分建立在超过50万个由兽医评分和训练的视频基础上，体况评分则基于专家评估者提供的110万个摄像头视图，”Mozeliak说。“因此，我们相信这项技术已经得到验证，而且我们已经拥有它，新西兰的奶农一直在告诉我们它有多神奇，以及它带来的改变。”

从卡车、拖拉机驾驶室或世界任何地方，牧场主都可以通过每头奶牛离开挤奶环节后收集的视频查看牛群情况。这些视频还可以与兽医、农场员工或任何可能需要根据早期检测信号采取行动的人分享。

据Mozeliak称，新西兰一家农业咨询公司进行了一项独立分析，考察了Darnley Dairy安装Herd-i前后的三个奶牛季节。研究发现，需要跛行治疗的奶牛减少了38%，专门用于跛行的抗生素治疗减少了41%。这相当于平均每季节减少82头需要治疗的奶牛和减少40次抗生素治疗。

“我们都知道，当你能够更快地处理一头奶牛并提供侵入性更小、成本更低的治疗时，它们的生产能力得以保持，结果就是奶罐里会有更多牛奶，”Mozeliak说。

Mozeliak表示，Herd-i不仅让农场的财务状况朝着积极方向发展，还可以减少精神压力，尤其是在繁忙季节。

**融入创新**

继9月在美国推出后，Herd-i正在提供“创始农场”计划。通过该计划，25个农场将获得免费安装和折扣订阅费率。

作为交换，Herd-i希望获得反馈，帮助完善技术以适应美国奶牛场，并塑造产品的未来。

“我们正在寻找那些不仅热衷于将跛行和体况评分产品带到自己农场，还愿意帮助担任大使的牧场主。这些关系很重要，”Mozeliak说。

该计划与新西兰的一个计划类似，当时一群奶农帮助塑造了技术解决农场挑战的方式。

虽然该技术目前是为奶牛设计的，但Mozeliak表示她认为它最终也有潜力服务于肉牛行业。

“Herd-i的未来在与奶农的对话中看起来非常光明。他们对热应激、温度和体重相关的额外信息非常感兴趣，”Mozeliak说。“其中很多事情目前他们必须手动跟踪。”

通过自动化这些任务，生产者已经表现出对这项技术的强烈兴趣。无论是因为人眼错过了这些细微线索，还是农场 simply 缺乏多余劳动力，这些摄像头都可以填补农场运营中的空白。

有兴趣了解更多关于Herd-i或加入创始农场计划的牧场主可以访问herd-i.com。
contentHtml: New Zealand-based company enters the U.S. dairy market with technology that scores lameness and body condition at every milking.
